Runs locally with consent acknowledgement and no upload

rising.description: 🔎 Username, email & phone OSINT — 9,700+ lookup checks from 19 projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs and expert-reviewed updates.

Windows installer, PyPI package and source install options
Evidence graph and PDF reporting for investigations

Claims of weekly expert review are unverified marketing

rising.description: Async, plugin-based OSINT recon for usernames, emails, phones, names & domains — 260+ sources, evidence-linked accounts, confidence-scored. Linux · macOS · Windows

Distinguishes confirmed from probable results
Multiple export formats and config checks
risks: Person lookup and breach checks raise privacy concerns
Mentions adult-site checks and optional holehe registration checks
Broad claims like 260+ sources not independently verified

Produces source-cited reports with recorded example output
Open source with a tests badge and a stated release version

Profile and comment extraction could be used to build dossiers on individuals
Heavy reliance on a separate socai CLI and an OpenRouter key

rising.description: Work out where and when an audio recording was made using only the thunder in it.

Installable via pip, cargo, or prebuilt binaries with documented inputs and outputs

Accuracy limits depend on recording and data quality; findings should be treated as probabilistic

rising.description: Public-data OSINT for emails, usernames, domains and companies: free sources, LLM briefing, colour report

Explicit safety section: no logins, no paid brokers, retry and quota handling
Documents limitations and reports unavailable sources
risks: Personal breach and email lookups could be used for doxxing if misused
Relies on LLM summaries that may overstate weak signals
Repository owner account and CI links are unverified; newly published project

rising.description: 86-tool OSINT MCP server with private evidence graphs, image analysis, reverse search, and person dossiers.
rising.summary: A Python stdio MCP server exposing 86 OSINT tools for DNS, domains, IPs, websites, public accounts, breach metadata, threat feeds, and images, with a private persistent evidence graph and person dossiers.
strengths: Broad tool coverage across several OSINT domains in one server
Install steps, client configuration, and verification command are documented
Works largely without API keys
risks: Person dossiers and breach metadata lookups raise privacy concerns
Breadth of 86 tools may indicate thin per-tool depth; not verified
README is marketing-heavy in places

rising.description: Local-First OSINT & Intelligence Investigation Platform
rising.summary: Electron desktop app for OSINT investigations. Maps entities and relationships on a force-directed graph, attaches cited evidence, runs transforms and link discovery, and stores cases as local Markdown files.

Force-directed graph with verification states for links
Relationship discovery and transforms with named features
risks: Discovery of shared phones, emails and tax IDs could enable personal-data linking on individuals
Built-in transforms and API console depend on third-party services whose terms vary
Limited details on legal or ethical use guidance

Documents steps and a report output for law enforcement

Recovery-scam adjacency; claims about exchange freezing outcomes are unverified

Clear method explanation and limitations section
Bilingual documentation and CI badge

Method derived from a video with no released code; independent implementation
Requires careful responsible-use framing to avoid misuse against individuals

rising.description: Scrape Facebook GraphQL data without an API key — profiles, posts, comments, reactions, groups, marketplace, search_engine.

Auto-recovers changed GraphQL Doc IDs without a headless browser
risks: Uses personal session cookies and likely violates Facebook terms of service
Lead-generation framing suggests bulk collection of personal data
Abandonment risk from reliance on undocumented internal endpoints

rising.description: Locate an audio or video recording from the Doppler curves of propeller aircraft, matched against archived ADS-B flight tracks. Rust, on frankenscipy and asupersync.

Pre-release alpha with a single validated real case
Pinned nightly toolchain may hinder reproducibility

rising.description: Terminal-first local OSINT field workbench with rigorous evidence provenance. Cases, content-addressed evidence, origin clustering, contradiction candidates, honest tool catalogue. Local-first, no telemetry.

strengths: Hash-addressed, re-verifiable evidence chain
Honest feature matrix and limitations documented
Local-first with no telemetry
risks: Alpha status (v0.1.0), pre-release
Username checks cover a small provider set

Offline date decoding from snowflake IDs

Self-hosted with documented install and verification guide

Pre-release version (v0.9.1) with limited maturity signals

Free, MIT-licensed, and runs locally without an account

strengths: Supports many networks (TON, TRON, Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana and more)
Interactive graphs with sourced evidence and checkpoints/resume
Separates established facts from analytical hypotheses
risks: Service attribution of wallets may be speculative
README is in Russian with limited English documentation
Mixed topic tags including unrelated celebrity names suggest keyword stuffing

disinformation.description: Open-source OSINT tool that detects coordinated influence campaigns across public Telegram channels, using near-duplicate text and image matching, burst detection and network analysis.
disinformation.summary: Open-source tool that collects public Telegram posts and detects coordinated influence campaigns using near-duplicate text and image matching, burst detection and network analysis, producing explainable scored reports.
strengths: Explainable scoring with named signals
Documented limitations and ethics section
Clear pipeline from collection to HTML/JSON reports
risks: Alpha status
Scores are leads, not verdicts; false positives from news aggregators
Paraphrased campaigns not detected

disinformation.description: Browser extension and web app that flags paid or planted sources in AI chatbot answers. Evidence, never a true/false verdict. English and Arabic.
disinformation.summary: Browser extension and web app that splits AI chatbot answers into claims, hunts independent evidence, and profiles cited sources for GEO-style manipulation patterns such as paid or planted placement. Offers English and Arabic.
strengths: Measured false-positive and held-out tests published in README
Reproducible builds with SBOM and checksums
No telemetry and no runtime dependencies
risks: Heuristic source flagging can mislabel legitimate publishers despite stated tests
Relies on LLM and search components for the full pipeline

general.description: Public-data OSINT for emails, usernames, domains and companies: free sources, LLM briefing, colour report
general.summary: A Python CLI that gathers public data on emails, usernames, domains, companies, phones and Bitcoin addresses from free sources, then produces an LLM-written or offline rule-based risk briefing and a colour-coded report.
strengths: Named public sources and an offline mode with no model needed
Explicit safety section: no logins, no paid brokers, retry and quota handling
Documents limitations and reports unavailable sources
risks: Personal breach and email lookups could be used for doxxing if misused
Relies on LLM summaries that may overstate weak signals
Repository owner account and CI links are unverified; newly published project

general.description: 86-tool OSINT MCP server with private evidence graphs, image analysis, reverse search, and person dossiers.
general.summary: A Python stdio MCP server exposing 86 OSINT tools for DNS, domains, IPs, websites, public accounts, breach metadata, threat feeds, and images, with a private persistent evidence graph and person dossiers.
strengths: Broad tool coverage across several OSINT domains in one server
Install steps, client configuration, and verification command are documented
Works largely without API keys
risks: Person dossiers and breach metadata lookups raise privacy concerns
Breadth of 86 tools may indicate thin per-tool depth; not verified
README is marketing-heavy in places

general.description: Cognitive digital twins and behavioral modeling for AI agents.
general.summary: A Python toolkit that builds cognitive digital twins of people from public articles, transcripts, podcasts and papers, then offers a Python SDK, MCP server and CLI for dialogue, scenario simulation and drift analysis.
strengths: Installable package with CLI, SDK and MCP server entry points
Documents pipeline stages and sources such as RSS, PDF and YouTube ingestion
MIT license with CI badge
risks: Builds psychological profiles of named individuals, raising ethical and privacy concerns
Claims of mathematical calibration and epistemic grounding are not backed by detail in the README
Output quality and legal limits for profiling people are not described

general.description: Does their story hold up? Paste what a seller, recruiter or landlord told you and check it against public records in thirty seconds, with proof saved for every reason.
general.summary: A Windows desktop app that takes a seller, recruiter or landlord's story, checks it against about 3,400 public sources in roughly 30 seconds, gives a verdict with reasons, and saves timestamped, hashed proof for each finding.
strengths: Saves snapshots, timestamps and SHA-256 hashes as evidence for each finding
Free, MIT-licensed, and runs locally without an account
risks: Marketing-heavy README; the 3,400+ source claim is not itemised in the visible text
Person lookups on private individuals could be misused for profiling; no legal or consent guidance is visible
Data sources section and build details are not shown in the digest, so verification of claims is limited

general.summary: A browser-based suite of about 20 free OSINT tools, including Google dork generation, username checks across websites, email analysis, breach lookups, and domain and certificate lookups using public APIs.
strengths: Many named public data sources
Browser-first design keeps uploaded files local
Explicit passive-only stance and credits
risks: Username and breach lookups on individuals carry privacy misuse potential
README digest is truncated, limiting verification

general.description: OTInstaller Registry: a free registry of OSINT tools and guides
general.summary: OTInstaller is a CLI package manager and registry for over 130 OSINT tools and investigation guides. It installs, runs, updates and removes tools in sandboxed containers or virtualenvs, stores API keys in one keychain, and saves results as JSON.
strengths: Concrete CLI commands and documented workflow
Sandboxed execution with signed checksums and cosign verification
Consistent typed inputs and JSON output across tools
risks: Tool breadth depends on third-party tools that may break or be abandoned
Install scripts piped to shell from a remote domain
Claims of scanning and nightly testing are not independently verifiable

general.description: ⚒️ Open-source OSINT and digital forensics skills for AI assistants. Investigate sources, challenge hypotheses, analyze artifacts, and produce evidence-referenced reports with portable case files and offline Python tools. Designed for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI.
general.summary: A set of 16 OSINT and digital forensics skills for AI assistants (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI) with offline Python tools for source preservation, hypothesis testing, evidence-referenced reporting and case handoff.
strengths: Offline Python standard library with no telemetry or mandatory provider
Evidence preservation with citations and correction history
Exports to GraphML and Timesketch-compatible CSV
risks: README excerpt is truncated; specific data sources are not visible
Breadth of 16 skills may mean uneven depth per skill

general.description: Modular OSINT workstation builder for Linux and Apple Silicon: guided menus, case audit trails, and public-records searches for 17 countries
general.summary: Shell-based installer that sets up a Debian, Ubuntu, Kali, Parrot or macOS machine with OSINT tools, guided menus, per-case folders with audit trails, and country public-records searches for 17 countries.
strengths: Modular, idempotent install with --only and --skip options
Case intake records and hash-chained notes with audit trail
Documented platform support and install commands
risks: Country public-records searches may touch personal data, so legal use matters
Broad scope spanning many tools makes maintenance and vetting harder
Recent rename and version claims cannot be independently verified

general.description: Modular Local-First OSINT Aggregator & Forensic Analyzer for Android (AES-256-GCM / Material Design 3)
general.summary: Android app that runs IP and phone-number lookups in parallel, combining an offline analyser with a configurable pool of external REST/JSON OSINT APIs. Keys and scan history are stored encrypted on the device, and it ships with 16 preset modules.
strengths: Local-first design with no intermediary servers, per the README
Documents a preset module catalogue and a JSON schema for custom API imports
Includes build instructions and Android Lint checks
risks: Phone and IP lookups against third-party APIs could be used to profile individuals
Many README sections are headings only, so detail is uneven

general.description: Passive, source-first OSINT notebook for Android and Windows: 22 public sources, evidence-linked findings, rule-based and optional local or cloud AI analysis, template-based PDF reports, 9 languages.
general.summary: Android and Windows OSINT notebook that queries 22 public sources (DNS, RDAP, Wayback, GitHub, Wikidata, threat feeds) for domains, IPs, organisations and hashes, keeps evidence-linked findings, runs rule-based or optional AI analysis, and exports PDF/HTML/CSV/JSON reports.
strengths: Evidence records and source links for every finding
Key-free sources work out of the box, with setup docs for keyed ones
Local-first with no telemetry; supports offline local models
risks: Optional cloud AI APIs may send investigation data off device
Early releases (v0.1.0, web-v0.2.2) suggest immature project

geospatial-imagery.description: Python tool for aircraft Doppler audio geolocation using historical ADS-B flight data (Source-available)
geospatial-imagery.summary: DOPPLERGEIST geolocates audio recordings by matching aircraft Doppler signatures against historical ADS-B flight data. It offers a Python CLI and a local browser interface, with automatic acoustic event discovery and ranked candidate locations.
strengths: Concrete method with named data sources (ADSB.lol archives)
Documented validation example with measured error
Provides CLI and local browser interface
risks: Source-available PolyForm Noncommercial license limits reuse
Accuracy claims rest on a single historical example

geospatial-imagery.description: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.
geospatial-imagery.summary: An agent skill that estimates where a photo was taken by combining EXIF, OCR, reverse image search, OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view, showing its reasoning as a candidate board.
strengths: Clear multi-stage pipeline with named scripts and data sources
Works across several agent platforms with install commands
Shows evidence and reasoning for each candidate location
risks: Reverse image search depends on Chrome or Playwright automation
Benchmark and limits detail is limited in the excerpt

geospatial-imagery.description: Find out where an audio recording was made. Planes flying past leave a faint engine hum whose pitch drops as they go by. AeroDoppler compares those pitch changes with public records of where planes actually flew, and works out where the microphone must have been.
geospatial-imagery.summary: Local-first research tool that estimates where a stationary audio recording was made by matching aircraft engine Doppler patterns against historical ADS-B flight trajectories, outputting ranked hypotheses with a relative fit score.
strengths: Novel acoustic side-channel geolocation method with documented methodology
Honest benchmarks and stated limitations
Runs locally with consent acknowledgement and no upload
risks: Research software with self-described unflattering results
Could be misused to locate recordings of others despite consent gating

geospatial-imagery.description: Work out where and when an audio recording was made using only the thunder in it.
geospatial-imagery.summary: Rust/Python CLI that estimates where and when an audio recording was made by matching thunder timing in the audio against MET Norway Frost lightning strike data, producing a probability map and HTML report.
strengths: Clear, novel geolocation method with simulation and evaluation workflow
Installable via pip, cargo, or prebuilt binaries with documented inputs and outputs
risks: Depends on a free Frost API key and external data service
Accuracy limits depend on recording and data quality; findings should be treated as probabilistic

geospatial-imagery.description: Locate where a recording was made from the Doppler curves of aircraft in its background, matched against ADS-B history. Agent skill + tested Python pipeline, English / 简体中文.
geospatial-imagery.summary: An agent skill and Python pipeline that estimates where an audio or video recording was made by fitting Doppler curves of background aircraft and matching them against historical ADS-B tracks. Includes synthetic blind-test accuracy results and documented limitations.
strengths: Tested Python pipeline with documented accuracy on synthetic blind tests
Clear method explanation and limitations section
Bilingual documentation and CI badge
risks: Can locate a recording's microphone position, which raises privacy and surveillance concerns
Method derived from a video with no released code; independent implementation
Requires careful responsible-use framing to avoid misuse against individuals

geospatial-imagery.description: Locate an audio or video recording from the Doppler curves of propeller aircraft, matched against archived ADS-B flight tracks. Rust, on frankenscipy and asupersync.
geospatial-imagery.summary: Rust CLI that estimates where an audio or video recording was made by fitting Doppler curves of propeller aircraft heard in it and matching them to archived ADS-B flight tracks, returning coordinates, confidence radius, map and nearest town.
strengths: Documented pipeline with offline selftest and doctor command
Explicit responsible-use guidance and credit to original method
Honest status section reporting validation limits
risks: Could be used to deanonymise location of recordings made by others
Pre-release alpha with a single validated real case
Pinned nightly toolchain may hinder reproducibility

geospatial-imagery.description: Identify the church tower heard in a recording from its bells' pitches.
geospatial-imagery.summary: Rust tool and Python package that identifies which church tower is audible in a recording by matching the spectral lines of its bells against Dove's Guide data, with optional geographic filtering and GPS metadata use.
strengths: Working CLI with documented options and JSON output
Reports accuracy on simulated and real recordings with stated limits
Uses a public, named bell database (Dove's Guide)
risks: Accuracy on real recordings is roughly one in three, so results are unreliable
Can geolocate a recording's location from its metadata GPS position, a privacy-relevant capability

geospatial-imagery.description: Open-source intelligence and human-rights hub on North Korea: intel map, missile test explorer, leadership graph, camps and verified data.
geospatial-imagery.summary: Open-source hub on North Korea offering an intel map with camps, missile sites, ports and satellite layers, a missile test explorer, leadership graph, sanctions data and weekly-refreshed sources, all with citations.
strengths: Maps sourced satellite imagery and open datasets
Weekly automated source checks via GitHub Actions
Multilingual, Apache 2.0 licensed
risks: Political advocacy framing may affect neutrality of data
Limited detail on methodology for verifying data in README excerpt

geospatial-imagery.description: Find where a mountain photo was taken, without GPS, from its skyline (S.D.E.C.E.)
geospatial-imagery.summary: Command-line tool that estimates where a mountain photo was taken, without GPS, by matching the photo's skyline against skylines rendered from national and global terrain models. Includes demo, limitations and sources.
strengths: Clear, working CLI with a reproducible demo and example output
Documents terrain sources, licences, accuracy and limitations
Quantified evaluation results and comparison with a related tool
risks: README is partly a narrative with a truncated usage section
Built with heavy AI assistance; project maturity unclear
Requires large GPU-dependent downloads and setup

geospatial-imagery.description: Plane noise in a video can give away where it was filmed. Open replication of colsto's Doppler + ADS-B method with honest results, plus a Claude Code skill (/colsto, /flyover-check) that finds that sound in your video.
geospatial-imagery.summary: Replicates colsto's Doppler and ADS-B method to geolocate where a recording was made from plane noise, with blind webcam runs and a Claude Code skill (/colsto, /flyover-check) that checks videos before posting and makes a safe copy.
strengths: Documents results including misses and uses public ADS-B data
Provides a privacy-oriented skill to scrub location leaks from one's own videos
risks: Method can geolocate recording places of others' videos, a dual-use privacy concern
Early first public version; results still being added

identity-lookup.description: 🔎 Username, email & phone OSINT — 9,700+ lookup checks from 19 projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs and expert-reviewed updates.
identity-lookup.summary: Consensus is a Python CLI and GUI that runs username, email and phone lookups across about 9,700 site modules from 19 open-source projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs, PDF reports and an MCP server for AI assistants.
strengths: Large consolidated module set with a stated review process
Windows installer, PyPI package and source install options
Evidence graph and PDF reporting for investigations
risks: Mass username and email lookups can enable profiling of private individuals
Claims of weekly expert review are unverified marketing

identity-lookup.description: Async, plugin-based OSINT recon for usernames, emails, phones, names & domains — 260+ sources, evidence-linked accounts, confidence-scored. Linux · macOS · Windows
identity-lookup.summary: Async Python CLI that takes a username, email, phone or name and queries 260+ sites and APIs concurrently, correlates findings into linked identities, scores confidence, and exports terminal, JSON, CSV, HTML or graph reports.
strengths: Clear usage examples and install steps
Distinguishes confirmed from probable results
Multiple export formats and config checks
risks: Person lookup and breach checks raise privacy concerns
Mentions adult-site checks and optional holehe registration checks
Broad claims like 260+ sources not independently verified

identity-lookup.description: A responsible, open-source Instagram username availability scanner. Async CLI with bounded concurrency, rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, Docker and GitHub Actions support.
identity-lookup.summary: Async Python CLI that generates short Instagram usernames and checks public profile pages to flag names with no visible profile. Supports rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, and txt, json, or csv output. Results are candidates only and must be verified on Instagram.
strengths: Documents clear limitations and that results are not guaranteed claimable
Resumable checkpoints and conservative UNKNOWN classification
Concrete example run and multiple output formats
risks: Brute-force enumeration of platform accounts may conflict with Instagram terms of service
Usefulness for OSINT is limited; mainly a username availability tool
Scope is contestable since the purpose is registration availability rather than investigation

identity-lookup.description: Free OSINT app for Discord IDs: paste a user, server or invite and see when it was made and who it copies.
identity-lookup.summary: Windows desktop app that decodes Discord snowflake IDs into creation dates and queries the official Discord API with your own bot token to show public profile, invite and server info, flagging look-alike copies of saved IDs and changed invites.
strengths: Uses official API with user's own bot token, no selfbot
Offline date decoding from snowflake IDs
Explicit legal notes on Discord ToS and trademarks
risks: Profile lookups of individuals could enable tracking or impersonation checks misuse
Build not code-signed; SmartScreen warning
Relies on Discord API which may restrict use

identity-lookup.description: GhostTrack 中文汉化版 | OSINT 追踪工具（IP/手机号/用户名）· 逻辑零改动纯汉化 · 原项目 HunxByts/GhostTrack
identity-lookup.summary: A translated Chinese-language version of the GhostTrack CLI. It looks up IP geolocation and ISP details, phone number metadata, and checks username existence across 24 social platforms. Logic is unchanged from upstream.
strengths: Clear menu-based CLI with documented install and run steps
Covers IP, phone and username lookups in one tool
Localized README and interface for Chinese-speaking users
risks: Upstream project has no open-source license, so redistribution rights are unclear
Derivative mirror of another author's work with stated copy-without-permission concerns
Username and phone lookups can support profiling of private individuals

identity-lookup.description: Local-first Windows OSINT tool for username and nickname research with evidence-aware, resumable, service-grouped results
identity-lookup.summary: Local-first Windows tool that searches public accounts for a single username or nickname, runs resumable jobs, groups results by service with evidence references, and exports HTML, text and JSON reports.
strengths: Local-first data handling with no hosted account required
Resumable jobs with checkpoints and service-grouped, evidence-labelled results
Explicit honesty about limits and non-identity-decision framing
risks: Username lookup across services can enable account profiling of individuals
Author states limited provider coverage and possible defects
Built with an LLM coding assistant; not fully understood by its author

identity-lookup.description: Desktop public username search, live results and site discovery. Python + pywebview.
identity-lookup.summary: NIX is a Windows and macOS desktop app that searches public profiles by username across a large catalog of sites, shows live results with reasons, filters by status, source and region, and discovers new sites from public directories. It exports results as JSON, CSV or HTML.
strengths: Clear, detailed README with described features, limits and usage steps
Live results and per-result reasons aid verification
Named upstream sources (Maigret, Sherlock, WhatsMyName)
risks: Username search across many sites can profile private individuals
Unsigned, non-notarized binaries
Adult sources and proxy use raise misuse considerations

identity-lookup.description: 🐉 sAScan — dragon-grade digital footprint intelligence. A stateless OSINT CLI that correlates usernames, emails and phone numbers into one interactive identity graph.
identity-lookup.summary: A stateless Python CLI that checks usernames, emails and phone numbers across 19 native platforms, optionally wraps Sherlock, Holehe and PhoneInfoga, correlates findings and renders an interactive HTML identity graph.
strengths: Stateless design with no stored scan history
Clear legal and ethical notice about authorized use
Documented verdicts and tests for core logic
risks: Profiles individuals by username, email and phone, enabling misuse for tracking
Relies on third-party tools for some capabilities
Early-stage project with limited evidence of maturity

identity-lookup.description: 🔍 把 Sherlock 跨站用户名查询封装成 Agent Skill：用法流程 + 命中核验 + 免责声明（基于 sherlock-project/sherlock）
identity-lookup.summary: A Chinese-language Agent Skill (SKILL.md) that wraps the Sherlock CLI for cross-site username searches. It adds install guidance, a two-step verification process for hits, usage limits and a disclaimer. It does not modify Sherlock's code.
strengths: Clear install path and known Python version pitfalls documented
Hit verification process distinguishes confirmed, blocked and false positives
States compliance boundaries and disclaimer
risks: Username lookup across hundreds of sites can enable profiling of individuals
Value is mostly documentation layered on an upstream tool

identity-lookup.description: A local, self-hosted web UI for GHunt — mxrch's OSINT framework for investigating Google accounts. ghunt-panel wraps the ghunt CLI in a small Flask app so you can run lookups, read the results, and manage your login session from a browser tab instead of a terminal.
identity-lookup.summary: A local Flask web panel that wraps the GHunt CLI so users can run Google account lookups (email, gaia id, drive, geolocate) and view results as cards, with session management in the browser.
strengths: Runs locally bound to 127.0.0.1, not exposed to network
Clear install and usage instructions
Renders results readably with full JSON available
risks: Requires user Google session credentials, a sensitive authentication method
Depends on upstream GHunt for all investigation logic
Enables Google account lookups on private individuals

knowledge.description: Continuously updated catalogue of open-source OSINT tools, skills, plugins, MCP servers, and agentic integrations.
knowledge.summary: A continuously updated, hand-reviewed awesome-list cataloguing open-source OSINT tools, MCP servers, agent skills and agentic integrations, organised by category and by target input, with CSV database and timeline.
strengths: Large catalogue of about 491 projects organised by category and input type
Maintained with recent update badge and multiple browsable indexes
risks: Catalogue only; links to third-party tools not verified here
Scope and quality depend on curation of external projects

knowledge.description: awesome-osint-arsenal 中文版：753 个 OSINT 与安全工具、50 个分类、一键安装脚本（译自 rawfilejson/awesome-osint-arsenal，MIT）
knowledge.summary: Simplified Chinese translation of awesome-osint-arsenal, a curated list of about 753 OSINT and security tools in 50 categories, with installer scripts for Debian, Ubuntu, Kali, and Termux.
strengths: Large categorized tool list with install commands
Named tools and one-command installers for several distributions
risks: Mostly a translated copy of an upstream list rather than original work
Security-offensive tools mixed into the install bundles, outside OSINT scope
Link and install freshness depends on ongoing maintenance

knowledge.description: OSINT tools and techniques — reconnaissance, investigation, threat intelligence
knowledge.summary: A multilingual curated list of OSINT tools grouped by category, including search engines, username and identity finders, reconnaissance frameworks, breach data checkers, media geolocation and phone or network intelligence.
strengths: Broad categorised coverage of OSINT tools
Multilingual README with a clear table layout
risks: Only a list of links with short descriptions, no usage detail
Some listed tools touch personal data and breach lookups, so the list itself carries misuse concerns
Language field left blank in the metadata; README language inferred as English

knowledge.description: In late September and early October of 2026 numerous Japanese organizations reported breaches and data leaks. This repository keeps track of such reports.
knowledge.summary: A dated, curated list of Japanese organisations reporting breaches and data leaks in 2026, with company profiles, impact notes, leaked data categories and source links.
strengths: Dated, structured entries with sources
Notes uncertainty explicitly with 'potentially' and 'possibly' phrasing
risks: Largely manual list with no tooling
Some entries are truncated and sources are sparse
Contains unverified claims about leaked personal data

knowledge.description: ADINT: a field guide to ad-tech surveillance. How advertising data (MAID, RTB bidstream, SDK location) becomes warrantless intelligence.
knowledge.summary: A field guide documenting how advertising data such as mobile ad IDs, RTB bidstream and SDK location feeds is used for surveillance. It catalogues data brokers, vendors, government buyers, regulators, timelines and sources, with RSS feeds.
strengths: Structured roster of entities, glossary and timeline with cited public sources
Maintained sources list with RSS feeds for monitoring
risks: Content is a research compilation rather than a tool; limited executable functionality

knowledge.description: Country-by-country dossiers on the global surveillance industry, spyware vendors, state agencies and Palantir.
knowledge.summary: A Markdown research repository of country-by-country dossiers on the global surveillance industry, covering spyware vendors, state agencies, data brokers and Palantir. The README digest shows structure and badges but few concrete sources or methods.
strengths: Organised as per-country dossiers with a clear topic scope
Covers vendors, state agencies and data brokers in one place
risks: Coverage section is empty in the README digest
Digest shows little on sourcing or verification methodology

media-forensics.description: Proof of concept that estimates where a recording was made from background thunder and propeller-aircraft sounds, matched against public lightning and ADS-B data. Built to show how audio leaks location, and what does and doesn't prevent it.
media-forensics.summary: Open-source proof of concept that estimates where an audio recording was made by matching thunder against public lightning records (GOES GLM) and aircraft Doppler against ADS-B flight tracks. Includes a CLI, a desktop UI, and validation results on real recordings.
strengths: Documents real-world validation results, including failures
Clear data sources and licence attribution
Working install path with an offline demo
risks: Demonstrates a method for locating a person's recordings, which could be misused for location inference
Alpha status, with only one of ten real thunder cases located

media-forensics.description: Is this video really new? IndexReel finds earlier uploads of a video and shows the frames side by side. Open-source X bot @askIndexReel, built with Meta's SSCD and Muse Spark.
media-forensics.summary: IndexReel checks whether a video is new by finding earlier uploads of it and shows matching frames side by side. It counts separate recordings behind a set of video posts, uses Meta's SSCD for frame matching and Muse Spark for verification, and runs as an open-source X bot.
strengths: Clear provenance and copy-detection purpose with documented pipeline steps
Reports test results and error rates for its matching model
risks: Relies on LLM verification and claim suggestions that may err
Bot replies on X could be misread as authoritative fact-checks

media-forensics.description: Trace file provenance, metadata, telemetry, investigative pivots and relationships across files, browser history, OS traces and archives. Local, read-only, no network requests.
media-forensics.summary: Local, read-only CLI that examines files for provenance, embedded metadata, C2PA, browser and OS traces, and investigative identifiers, correlating findings into an evidence graph with exports.
strengths: Local and read-only with no network requests during analysis
Clear evidence sources and supported formats documented
Corroboration and conflict tracking with source attribution
risks: Pivot extraction can surface personal identifiers such as accounts, financial and geographic data
Feature-heavy README; real-world maturity not independently verified

media-forensics.description: Open-source, cross-platform document discovery & metadata reconnaissance tool  a modern, Windows-free alternative to FOCA.
media-forensics.summary: Python CLI and local web UI that discovers PDF and Office documents on target domains via crawling, sitemaps, Wayback Machine and search dorking, then extracts metadata with ExifTool to report leaked usernames and other data.
strengths: Clear FOCA-style purpose with named sources and tools
Cross-platform install instructions for macOS, Linux and Windows
Documented CLI, web UI, REST API and Docker options
risks: Can expose authors and internal usernames of target organisations, a potential misuse vector
Optional PII content scanning and sensitive-file discovery broaden scope

situational-awareness.description: Wireshark for the radio spectrum: channelize a wide span once, decode every signal in it at once
situational-awareness.summary: Desktop SDR tool that channelizes a wide radio band and decodes many signal types at once, including ISM devices, ADS-B, AIS, APRS, pagers, DMR, TETRA, LoRa and radiosondes, with recording and an agent option.
strengths: Decodes many protocols from one wide-band capture
Named decoders and bands with a clear install path
Passive reception of public transmissions
risks: Intercepting TETRA and DMR traffic with decryption and key recovery raises legal concerns
Records voice and messages, which may capture private communications
Agent can transmit on radio, requiring licensing awareness

situational-awareness.description: Real-time situational-awareness dashboard for Hong Kong - one map, many official open data sources, no API keys in the client. Open source (AGPL-3.0); not a government system.
situational-awareness.summary: Browser-based live map dashboard consolidating Hong Kong government and institutional open data (traffic cameras, weather, transport, border waits, aircraft positions, markets) with each reading linked to its publisher. Static app with a whitelisted Cloudflare Worker proxy.
strengths: Clear source catalogue with endpoints, cadence and licence in SOURCES.md
Every reading traceable to its publisher
No API keys in client bundle
risks: Mostly a civic dashboard; OSINT framing is light
Proxy routes third-party data, so upstream terms must be respected

situational-awareness.description: Strażnik — nieoficjalne wczesne ostrzeganie o zagrożeniach powietrznych dla Polski. Fuzja sygnałów NEPTUN, mediów, RCB, ADS-B i PAŻP + aplikacja Android.
situational-awareness.summary: Unofficial early-warning tool for air threats over Poland. It fuses NEPTUN signals, media reports, RCB alerts, ADS-B aircraft data and PAŻP inputs into a map with an Android app and FastAPI backend.
strengths: Names concrete official and open data sources
Has a backend run section and a full user manual
Actively maintained with frequent versioned releases
risks: README is mostly release notes in Polish with little usage detail
Unofficial alert system; users may rely on it for safety decisions
Depends on third-party ADS-B API quotas and fallback sources

situational-awareness.description: Earth-centered OSINT workspace with attributed source reports, regional tracking, replay and bounded local briefings.
situational-awareness.summary: An Earth-centred Cesium workspace for conflict monitoring: attributed source reports from RSS and other feeds, regional tracking, replay, and bounded local AI briefings. Includes a keyless synthetic showcase; live Google imagery needs a restricted key and billing.
strengths: Keyless showcase lets users try the interface without credentials
Retains citations and revision history for reports
Explicit limits on imagery coverage and dates
